name: Kestrel Dynamics BlastSeal EOD Response Suit
description: Matte olive-drab with high-vis orange panel inserts at the torso and thighs, the BlastSeal is a full-body explosive ordnance disposal suit that moves like wearing a building. The outer shell is multi-ply ballistic nylon over rigid ceramic-composite trauma plates at chest, abdomen, and thighs — the plates are removable via Velcro-sealed access panels. An integrated ballistic collar and neck brace assembly locks into the helmet ring. The suit's arms are heavily padded, limiting fine motor control. Interior cooling tubes run from a spine-mounted micro-chiller unit. Kestrel's raptor-wing crest is embossed on both shoulders.
functionality: Rated for fragmentation and overpressure from devices up to Class-4 detonation at 1.5m standoff. Micro-chiller sustains safe internal temperature for 90-minute operational windows. Spinal rig channel allows limited BCI integration for remote sensor feeds. Mobility is severely restricted — suit weight is 34kg without helmet.
what_it_says: You walk toward the thing everyone else is running from, and the city pays you just enough to almost feel worth it.
story_hooks: A BlastSeal recovered from a CorpSec depot has had its serial number ground off and a Shelf gang's territorial mark scratched into the collar ring — someone stole it, and they're using it for something other than bomb disposal.
The micro-chiller spine unit is a known point of failure — a coolant leak at 60 minutes has killed three technicians; Kestrel has suppressed the maintenance reports.
An EOD specialist who survived a Class-5 detonation in this suit claims the ceramic plates fused to her chrome arm — the suit saved her life and cost her the limb.

physical_description.visual_profile: A heavily armored, utilitarian silhouette that reads as industrial and imposing. The matte olive-drab base is interrupted by bold high-vis orange panels at the torso and thighs, creating a stark safety-first aesthetic. The wearer appears broader, more geometric, almost architectural in presence.
physical_description.fit: Rigid and oversized for maximum armor accommodation. The suit prioritizes protection over mobility, creating a boxy, squared-off profile that restricts natural movement. Arms are noticeably stiff and padded; torso is heavily reinforced.
physical_description.primary_material: Multi-ply ballistic nylon exterior over rigid ceramic-composite trauma plates; interior moisture-wicking synthetic blend; reinforced spine-mounted polymer housing for chiller unit
physical_description.texture: Matte, weathered nylon with a slightly rough finish; ceramic plates visible through semi-transparent access panels; ribbed padding along arms and shoulders; smooth integrated tubing at collar assembly
physical_description.color_scheme: Matte olive-drab as dominant color; high-vis international orange at torso and thighs for visibility and regulatory compliance; dark charcoal at collar and arm reinforcements
physical_description.closures: Heavy-duty Velcro-sealed access panels for armor plate removal; integrated magnetic snap closures at shoulders; friction-fit helmet ring assembly; sealed micro-chiller dock at spine
distinctive_features: Removable ceramic-composite trauma plates at chest, abdomen, thighs via Velcro panels
Integrated ballistic collar and rigid neck brace assembly
Spine-mounted micro-chiller unit with interior cooling tube network
Kestrel Dynamics raptor-wing crest embossed on both shoulders
Helmet ring locking mechanism at neck assembly
High-vis orange safety panels meeting EOD protocol standards
Reinforced arm padding limiting fine motor control
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 1-2 luxury/military — this is corporate defense equipment, expensive and purpose-built, accessible only to authorized military, corporate security, or government EOD teams
physical_description.cultural_context: Military-industrial, government contractor, hazmat/EOD specialist. Wearing this signals professional training, danger-proximity work, and corpo-military affiliation. In civilian contexts, it reads as ex-military or active threat-response personnel.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine to lightly weathered depending on deployment history. Dust and scuff marks common; ceramic plates may show impact signatures; cooling tubes may have visible condensation; Velcro panels show repeated use wear
